rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> field experiment on a 0.2 ha farmer's field at Akaltyn, 2006<U+2013>2007, with measured soil moisture, ECe, groundwater depth and yields used to calibrate/validate SWAP. Q2: Results (Fig. 3, Fig. 4, Table IV) <U+2013> SWAP checked against measured soil moisture (RMSE 0.012<U+2013>0.027), measured ECe and measured yields (simulated within 5%); Table IV reports WPT (0.66, 0.75 kg m-3) and WPET (0.52, 0.58 kg m-3) from model transpiration/ET and measured yields; Scenario analysis (Fig. 9, Conclusions) <U+2013> simulated irrigation regimes 175<U+2013>400 mm at 200 cm water table show yields rise to ~3.0 t ha-1 at 250 mm with only 3<U+2013>5% further gain above that, i.e. 250 mm identified as the adequate amount. Q4: Table IV and Figs 7<U+2013>8 <U+2013> model quantifies soil evaporation (~30% of ETpot, stated as major reason for low WP), actual transpiration, bottom flux/capillary rise from groundwater and root zone salinity as the intermediate variables linking irrigation amount and water table to yield/WP. Q7: Scenario analysis and Conclusions <U+2013> the ~3.0 t ha-1 at 250 mm holds only with groundwater table kept at ~200 cm (drains able to maintain that depth); reaching potential yields of 4<U+2013>6 t ha-1 requires leaching with fresh water and rehabilitation of the drainage network; irrigations must be applied in small amounts to avoid water table rise bringing salts into the root zone. Q8: Results and Scenario analysis <U+2013> measured ECe available for only 2<U+2013>3 days per year; differences in soil moisture attributed to profile heterogeneity and observation error; SWAP ignores nutrition, pests and disease; findings stated as representative only of the current salinity situation of the area; crop production not exclusively determined by water table depth.
rows.notes: Q2 given with some doubt: the WP/scheduling result rests on a scenario analysis (irrigation amounts <U+00D7> water table depth) whose outputs are not themselves measured, but the model was calibrated and validated against soil moisture, salinity and yield measurements from the same field, so it is treated as checked against observations. The scenarios vary seasonal amount with a fixed schedule rather than timing. Q3: one method (field-calibrated SWAP) <U+2013> measured yields serve as validation, not an independent estimate of the scheduling effect. Q5/Q6: one field, one crop, one site. Q9: only RMSE and a within-5% yield agreement are given; the 'within standard deviation of measured values' statement refers to measured ECe for validation, not to dispersion of the WP/yield scenario result.

notes: Full text available; figures are referenced but not reproduced in the text. The study's own measured WP values are for existing practice; the 'potential for increasing WP' is inferred from model scenarios on irrigation amount and water table depth plus a discussion of soil evaporation losses.
